subject: Proposal: midterm capacity uplift & co-term to Jan 1 renewal
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah@ravendocs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage spike & request: mid-contract uplift + co-term to Jan 1 renewal

Hey Ben,

Hope you had a good week — quick one from our side. We saw an unexpected Q3 usage spike tied to a new customer integration; over the last 6 weeks consumption is ~40% above our committed monthly baseline. We're 7 months into our current term and the overage is starting to impact our production plans.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide options to add mid-contract capacity (short-term top-up or annualize the uplift) and how that would be billed/prorated?
- We want to align the added capacity to our renewal on Jan 1, 2027. Is there a co-term path that avoids multiple invoices and gives better economics if we annualize starting Jan?

We need a ballpark by next Tue (9/14) to plan with finance. I've attached a short usage export for context (RavenDocs_usage_Q3.csv). Happy to run through numbers — Alex from infra is on copy.

Thanks —
Sarah Park
Head of ML Ops
RavenDocs
attachments: RavenDocs_usage_Q3.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@ravendocs.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage spike & request: mid-contract uplift + co-term to Jan 1 renewal

Sarah — thanks for the heads-up and the CSV, that helps. High-level thoughts:

Option A — Short-term top-up (fast):
- Immediate burst/top-up for the remainder of the quarter (prorated daily).
- No change to renewal on Jan 1; billed as overage + one-off top-up invoice.
- Good if you need speed.

Option B — Staged annualize (recommended if you expect sustained lift):
- Convert the uplift to a committed add-on starting now but annualize on Jan 1 (pro-rate the remainder of 2026, full year rates start 1/1/27).
- Provide a stepped discount on the new committed volume (we can offer a discount tier once you annualize).

I'll run numbers back-of-envelope now and follow up with concrete pricing. If you prefer, we can draft a short amendment to the contract + a DocuSign flow to capture acceptance.

Quick Qs:
- Is the 40% increase expected to hold through Q4, or is it an ephemeral integration test?
- Are you comfortable with a small committed uplift that auto-renews at co-term?

Putting Monica on copy to coordinate pricing and any finance constraints.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:09:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Usage spike & request: mid-contract uplift + co-term to Jan 1 renewal

Monica / Kimberly — forwarding RavenDocs thread. Key facts: Q3 usage +40% vs baseline, want co-term to Jan 1 and ballpark pricing by 9/14 (they asked earlier; timeline slips but still urgent).

My initial thinking (numbers are rough):
- Baseline commitment: 100k token-equivalent units/mo (example). Current usage now ~140k.
- Option 1 (short-term top-up): add 40k units monthly for remainder of 2026 at list prorated -> est incremental $18k for Q4.
- Option 2 (annualize to co-term): commit to +40k units on Jan 1, 12-month term; offer 8% discount on incremental volume if they sign amendment + DocuSign by Oct 1. Pro-rate Oct-Dec at discounted rate on signing.

Questions for you:
- Finance: is 8% acceptable for a 12-month add-on if we require commit and no earlier churn? Any minimums we should insist on?
- Pricing: would a stepped discount (5% immediately, 8% if annualized) be a cleaner pitch?

Goal: get to a clean 2–3 option email to the customer with exact $s and a DocuSign link.

Thanks —
Ben

Subject: Re: Fwd: Usage spike & request: mid-contract uplift + co-term to Jan 1 renewal

Ben — quick finance take. We can support a promotional structure that encourages annualization while protecting revenue:

Counterproposal to present:
- Option A (fast top-up): one-off add of 40k units for Q4, billed prorated at list. No discount.
- Option B (staged annualize):
  - Sign amendment by Oct 1. Immediate pro-rated charge for Oct–Dec at a 5% introductory discount on the uplift.
  - On Jan 1 become annual commitment for the uplift with a 10% discount on the incremental volume for the 12-month term.
  - If they cancel within the 12 months, standard termination clauses apply; no retro credits.

This gives them quick relief and a clear incentive to annualize. From finance POV, the Jan 1 start + 10% discount is acceptable if we have an amendment signed and a 12-month minimum. I can draft the amendment language.

I attached a short calc sheet (internal) to show gross-to-net impact.

Monica
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposal (3 options) for RavenDocs: Q4 uplift & co-term path to Jan 1 renewal

Hi Sarah / Alex — thanks again for the usage export and patience while we scoped options. Below are three paths; pick the one that best fits RavenDocs' runway and procurement preferences and we will send a short amendment + DocuSign link.

Option 1 — Immediate top-up (fastest)
- Add 40k units/month for remainder of 2026 (Oct–Dec), prorated on Oct 1.
- Billed as a one-off top-up invoice at list rate. Estimated Q4 incremental charge: $18,400.
- No change to current Jan 1 renewal.

Option 2 — Staged annualize (balanced) [recommended]
- Sign amendment by Oct 1. Charge pro-rated Oct–Dec at a 5% discount on uplift.
- On Jan 1, uplift converts to a 12-month commitment; incremental uplift receives 10% discount for the 12-month term.
- Estimated incremental first-year spend (pro-rated + annualized) at discounted rates: $72,000 (illustrative).

Option 3 — Immediate annualize (simple billing)
- Convert uplift to annual commitment effective Oct 1 with a 6-month pro-rate to align billing to Jan 1; 8% discount on incremental volume if signed by Sep 30.
- One invoice covers remainder of 2026 + full 2027 commitment pro-rated accordingly.

Next steps:
- Tell me which option you prefer and I will route an amendment to your procurement team.
- For Option 2/3 we can provide a DocuSign link; for Option 1 we’ll issue a top-up invoice.

Attachments: RavenDocs_MAAP_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal + simple SOW), RavenDocs_usage_Q3.csv (your export).

Proposed authorizing signature path: Sarah (accept) -> Alex (technical signoff) -> procurement. If you'd like, I can also set up a quick 20-min call to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
